ada.answer: A stock review should record lead time because it shows how long it takes for an order to arrive, which determines when replenishment must be placed. It should also record a reorder threshold so the team knows the inventory level at which a new order is triggered. Together, lead time and reorder threshold help prevent stockouts, reduce excess inventory, and make purchasing decisions more timely and reliable.

A stock review should record lead time because it shows how long it takes for an order to arrive after it is placed, which determines how much inventory must be on hand to cover demand during that window. It should also record the reorder threshold so the team knows the exact stock level at which a new order should be placed, rather than relying on memory or guesswork. Together, lead time and reorder threshold make replenishment predictable, reduce stockouts and excess inventory, and give managers a clear basis for reviewing whether stock levels are adequate.
